references.text: The same prohibition against approaching the mountain was given during the first legislation on Sinai, where both people and animals were forbidden to touch the mountain.
The Lord warned Moses to set boundaries around the mountain so that the people would not break through to see the Lord and die.
On a previous occasion, Moses was told to come up to the Lord alone, while the others had to keep their distance.
The book of Hebrews refers to the terrifying experience at Mount Sinai, where even animals that touched the mountain were to be stoned.
Describes the same event and principle: The strict prohibition against approaching the holy mountain for both people and animals.
Directly related text: 19:12 sets the boundaries, while 34:3 confirms that no one (neither person nor animal) should be there.
